name: Carry Bit
description: Let $$$f(x,y)$$$ be the number of carries of $$$x+y$$$ in binary (i. e. $$$f(x,y)=g(x)+g(y)-g(x+y)$$$, where $$$g(x)$$$ is the number of ones in the binary representation of $$$x$$$). Given two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$, find the number of ordered pairs $$$(a,b)$$$ such that $$$0 \leq a,b \lt 2^n$$$, and $$$f(a,b)$$$ equals $$$k$$$. Note that for $$$a\ne b$$$, $$$(a,b)$$$ and $$$(b,a)$$$ are considered as two different pairs. As this number may be large, output it modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
input_specification: The only line of each test contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$0\leq k \lt n\leq 10^6$$$).
output_specification: Output a single integer  — the answer modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to N using Fermat's Little Theorem (mod 10^9+7 or 998244353). Answer nCr queries in O(1) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1761D — Carry Bit [310. Large Factorials and Binomial Coefficients]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Combinatorial selection $\binom{N}{K} = \frac{N!}{K!(N-K)!} \pmod P$ can be evaluated in $O(1)$ by precomputing factorials $fact[i] = fact[i-1] \cdot i \pmod P$ and inverse factorials $invFact[i] = invFact[i+1] \cdot (i+1) \pmod P$ using Fermat's Little Theorem $a^{P-2} \equiv a^{-1} \pmod P$.
